title: Natural bounded-below finite-cover etale hypercohomology descent
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $p:Z\to Y$ a finite surjective morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. All complexes are in the Grothendieck abelian category of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\Lambda$ on the small etale site, and all pullbacks are the exact inverse images [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image, lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]. Derived sections and cohomology mean the module-valued functors of [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. Let $a\in\mathbf Z$ and $K\in D^{\ge a}(Y_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $Z_q=Z^{\times_Y(q+1)}$ and $p_q:Z_q\to Y$. There is a natural augmentation quasi-isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(Y,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{q\ge0}R\Gamma(Z_q,p_q^*K).$$
Here the right hand side is represented by compatible bounded-below cochain resolutions, with internal degrees at least $a$ and Cech degree $q\ge0$, alternating coface differential $\delta$, and total differential $\delta+(-1)^q d$. The total has finite diagonals. Its Cech filtration gives a convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{q,j}=H^j(Z_q,p_q^*K)\Rightarrow H^{q+j}(Y,K)$ with $q\ge0$ and $j\ge a$, finite filtration on each abutment, and stationary terms in each bidegree. Negative $j$ are allowed.

For every morphism $h:Y'\to Y$, put $Z'=Y'\times_YZ$, $K'=h^*K$ and $Z'_q=Y'\times_YZ_q$. The restriction maps induce a morphism between these augmented resolved Cech diagrams. The square between $R\Gamma(Y,K)\to R\Gamma(Y',K')$ and the two totalizations commutes in $D(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$. Its column-$q$ map is precisely $R\Gamma(Z_q,p_q^*K)\to R\Gamma(Z'_q,(p'_q)^*K')$ induced by restriction. No assertion that this column map or its cohomology is an isomorphism is made.

source.place: Tag 09Z2, lemma-cohomological-descent-finite: exact augmented finite-cover resolution and its natural maps. Bounded-below constant-module and change-of-scheme extension by the same resolution construction, with finite diagonals; derivation in report.md.

proof.text: Represent $K\in D^{\ge a}$ by a complex $F$ with $F^j=0$ for $j<a$, using the equivalent strictly supported representative in the standard t-structure. Put $C_q=p_{q*}p_q^{-1}F$, with augmentation $C_{-1}=F$. Exact module inverse image identifies $p_q^{-1}F$ with $p_q^*K$ in the derived category. The module Čech augmentation lemma gives exactness of $0\to F^j\to C_0^j\to C_1^j\to\cdots$ for each $j$, before any injective replacement. Apply the augmentation quasi-isomorphism criterion to this unreplaced bicomplex, with complex index $s=j$ and resolution index $r=q$. Its rows are quasi-isomorphic to $F^j[0]$, and vanish for $j<a$. The map $F\to\operatorname{Tot}C$ is the augmentation into the $q=0$ diagonal summand, so the criterion gives a quasi-isomorphism. The total differential is $\delta+(-1)^q d$.

source.place: Tag 09Z2, exact augmented resolution; homology.tex Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution, applied to the unreplaced rows

proof.text: The category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(Y_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ is Grothendieck abelian, hence has functorial injective embeddings. Apply the bounded functorial injective-resolution theorem to choose one natural quasi-isomorphism $\eta:V\to I(V)$ on all bounded-below complexes. Set $J_q=I(C_q)$ and also $J_{-1}=I(F)$. Every $J_q^j$ is injective and is zero for $j<a$. Apply this single functor to each coface and codegeneracy, and then take alternating sums of the resulting cofaces to define the horizontal differential. The cosimplicial identities still hold, so its square is zero; each coface is a chain map, so it commutes with $d$. Naturality of $\eta$ gives a map of augmented bicomplexes $C\to J$. We do not assert exactness of the horizontal rows of $J$, or assume $I$ additive. The horizontal differential on $J$ is the sum of the resolved cofaces, not $I$ of their sum.

source.place: Tag 0141, lemma-functorial-injective-resolutions and remark-match; apply to the complete augmented cosimplicial diagram

proof.text: We now compare totals in the sheaf category $\mathcal A$, independently of exactness of the replaced rows. Form the double complex $E_q=\operatorname{Cone}(C_q\xrightarrow{\eta_q}J_q)$. Every vertical column is acyclic, and $E_q^j=J_q^j\oplus C_q^{j+1}$ vanishes for $j<a-1$. Translate the internal index by $a-1$ and apply the first spectral sequence of the double-complex theorem in the abelian category $\mathcal A$. Its $E_1$ page is zero, so its finite abutment filtration has zero graded pieces; hence $\operatorname{Tot}E$ is acyclic. Identify it with $\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}C\to\operatorname{Tot}J)$: on the summand in horizontal degree $q$, use $(b,c)\mapsto(b,(-1)^q c)$. Substituting in $\delta+(-1)^q d$ gives the ordinary cone differential, including the minus sign on the horizontal differential of the shifted $C$ summand. Thus $\operatorname{Tot}C\to\operatorname{Tot}J$ is a quasi-isomorphism of sheaf complexes. This only relabels the vertical degrees; the sign $(-1)^q$ is unchanged.

source.place: Tags 0130 and 0132: first spectral sequence in an arbitrary abelian category; cone-total signs written explicitly

proof.text: Consequently $F\to\operatorname{Tot}J$ is a quasi-isomorphism. In total degree $n$, only $0\le q\le n-a$ contribute, so $\operatorname{Tot}J$ is bounded below and has injective terms: for a monomorphism, extend a map to each of the finitely many injective summands and combine the extensions. The bounded-below-injectives clause of the K-injective theorem makes $\operatorname{Tot}J$ and $I(F)$ K-injective. Hence they compute $R\Gamma(Y,K)$. Their augmentation map is a quasi-isomorphism (its composite with $F\to I(F)$ is the preceding quasi-isomorphism), and the K-injective sections-comparison theorem shows that applying sections represents its derived isomorphism. Apply the additive mapped-total isomorphism to $\Gamma(Y,-)$ with indices $(s,r)=(j,q)$ and bound $s\ge a$: $\Gamma(Y,\operatorname{Tot}J)\cong\operatorname{Tot}_{q\ge0}\Gamma(Y,J_q)$. Each $J_q$ is a bounded-below injective resolution of $C_q$. The finite-pushforward module Leray identification gives $R\Gamma(Y,C_q)\cong R\Gamma(Z_q,p_q^{-1}F)$. This proves the stated augmentation quasi-isomorphism with compatible column representatives having internal degree at least $a$.

source.place: Tag 015J, lemma-two-ss-complex-functor, total and mapped-total remarks; bounded-below injective complexes are K-injective (the existing 079P node clause)

proof.text: Filter $\operatorname{Tot}\Gamma(Y,J)$ by Čech degree $q$. The filtered-complex construction has initial graded differential the vertical differential. Reindex $j$ as $j-a\ge0$ and apply the first double-complex spectral sequence in $\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda$. Under the finite-pushforward identifications of Step 4 its first page is $E_1^{q,j}=H^j(Z_q,p_q^*K)$, and the augmentation identifies its abutment with $H^{q+j}(Y,K)$. Translating the index back retains every integer $j\ge a$, including negative $j$ when $a<0$. The double-complex theorem supplies stabilization and a finite image filtration; explicitly in total degree $n$ the only possible horizontal indices satisfy $0\le q\le n-a$. This is relabeling of the vertical index and total degree, with the same differentials and the same sign $(-1)^q$. We invoke the theorem's convergence statement itself, not the argument of the module-only Čech cone lemma.

source.place: Tags 012K, 0130 and 0132; shifted first-quadrant double complex and finite image filtration

proof.text: For $h:Y'\to Y$, write $F'=h^{-1}F$, $C'_q=p'_{q*}(p'_q)^{-1}F'$, and $J'_q=I'(C'_q)$. Exact module inverse image keeps the bound $a$. Construct $b_q:h^{-1}C_q\to C'_q$ as the mate of the counit along the Cartesian square of $p_q$ and $h$, using $(p'_q)^{-1}h^{-1}=g_q^{-1}p_q^{-1}$ and $g_q^{-1}p_q^{-1}F=(p'_q)^{-1}h^{-1}F$. At the augmentation set $b_{-1}=\mathrm{id}_{F'}$. For a projection $r:Z_{q+1}\to Z_q$ and its base change $r'$, a section represented on an etale $U\to Y$ is sent by either composite to its pullback on $U'\times_{Y'}Z'_{q+1}$: the equality is $g_q r'=r g_{q+1}$, and functoriality of restriction gives equality of the two section maps. Such local representatives generate inverse image after sheafification, so this checks each coface square. Repeated-coordinate maps and the identity section give the identical check for codegeneracies and augmentation. We use these canonical mate maps only; their invertibility is not needed. Apply the resolved-diagram roof node to $A=C$, $B=C'$ and $b$. It supplies the actual coface-compatible zigzag $\Gamma I(C)\to\Gamma I'(h^{-1}I(C))\leftarrow\Gamma I'(h^{-1}C)\to\Gamma I'(C')$, including the augmentation. All its internal degrees are at least $a$.

source.place: Tag 0141 and remark-match; coface naturality of the Čech augmentation of etale-cohomology.tex Tag 09Z2; unit/counit mate construction

proof.text: The backward arrow in Step 6 is a quasi-isomorphism in each column. Apply the module-valued Čech cone-comparison statement to this very map: all column cones are acyclic, so its vanishing conclusion for every integer $r$ makes the cone on the total map acyclic. Thus the zigzag defines a morphism of the augmented total diagrams in $D(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$. At column $q$, the roof node identifies it with restriction along $h$ followed by $R\Gamma(b_q)$. The explicit unit/counit compatibility square in the finite-pushforward module Leray node identifies this composite with restriction along $g_q:Z'_q\to Z_q$. At augmentation degree $-1$ the same roof is precisely $R\Gamma(Y,K)\to R\Gamma(Y',h^*K)$. Each arrow of the roof already commutes with augmentation, so after inverting its backward total quasi-isomorphism the required square commutes. This is a roof of actual double-complex maps, so no choice of unrelated morphisms in the derived category of individual columns is totalized.

split_report.summary: Repaired every returned point: exact Čech rows are used only before replacement; bounded functorial injective resolutions preserve the common lower bound and all cofaces; the sheaf-level column-cone spectral sequence proves total comparison; finite-diagonal injective totals are K-injective; mapped-total and module-valued finite-pushforward Leray compute the columns. Base restriction is a common-resolution roof of actual augmented cosimplicial complexes with a columnwise quasi-isomorphic backward map. Its total comparison now applies the module cone node as a statement. The Leray support statement gives a precise canonical-mate compatibility square and needs no finite base-change isomorphism. Stale tool uses were removed and all off-unit proof tools declared.
split_report.blueprint: The finite-surjective Čech descent supporting lem-trf-local-term-locality through lem-trf-nearby-finite-base-descent: Steps 1–4 prove augmentation/derived totalization, Step 5 convergence with the original integer lower bound, Steps 6–7 restriction compatibility. Three retained support nodes give exact module augmentation, finite-pushforward comparison, and a generic resolved-diagram roof. The existing definition def-kun-rgamma-unbounded supplies module derived sections, so the duplicate sandbox definition was dropped.

They construct no arbitrary comparison. The theorem has one postponed proof and includes naturality in coefficients and arbitrary change of base, without asserting column restriction isomorphisms. ModuleCat-valued étale sheaves use the coefficient encoding of def-kun-rgamma-unbounded.
